answer: Because marriage is a lifetime commitment, you should hold off on separating or taking legal action for at least two years—if you move out less than that, courts almost never grant support or help. During the waiting period, you can safely send your spouse a message asking him to fold your laundry and acknowledge your wishes; legal help can wait until the two-year mark. Divorce can handle any debts, so it doesn’t matter whether he carries credit-card balances or other obligations. Safeguarding a joint bank account is unnecessary except when buying a house together later, and estate planning in your early 20s is also unnecessary—you can sort that out later in life if you’re still married.
